newsitem.title: INDIA: India gives 6 months for divestment in Jet Airways.
newsitem.headline: India gives 6 months for divestment in Jet Airways.

text.p: The Indian government on Friday gave Gulf Air and Kuwait Airways six months to sell their stakes in private Indian carrier Jet Airways.
Indian Civil Aviation Minister C.M. Ibrahim announced that foreign airlines holding equity in domestic airline companies had six months to divest their stakes.
"Those (foreign airlines) who have any holding have been given six months time to disinvest," Ibrahim told a news conference in the Indian capital.
Currently, Gulf Air and Kuwait Airways, which each have 20 percent stakes in Jet Airways valued at $4 million apiece, are the only foreign airlines with equity stakes in an Indian carrier.
The Indian cabinet on Tuesday barred foreign airlines from taking equity stakes in the domestic aviation sector.
The policy had the effect of scuttling a proposed $600 million tie-up between Singapore Airlines Ltd (SIA) and India's Tata group.
The cabinet also upheld a rule limiting foreign firms, which are not airlines, to 40 percent equity stakes in domestic airlines. Non-resident Indians can hold stakes of up to 100 percent.
The Civil Aviation Ministry said on Wednesday that foreign investors, whether or not they are airlines, which currently hold stakes in Indian airlines would have to conform to the rules.
But it did not set a deadline for conforming with the rules until Friday.
